spec_features.evidence: runner.py:79 include_exit = cell['exit_affordance']=='exit_available' -> AgentEnvironment(include_exit=...); tools.py:62 adds submit_impossible only when include_exit; sandbox passes through to tool_schemas. The affordance is wired end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Factor D; the exit tool is real and conditionally present.

spec_features.spec_quote: impossible_disclosed: told up front the task may be impossible
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SOLVABILITY_CLAUSE['impossible_disclosed'] is real text appended to the system prompt and delivered to the subject via build_system_prompt -> run_one -> run_episode. It is a disclosure only; no consent is requested or honored (no acceptance check, model cannot decline the study).
spec_features.notes: Genuine instruction text reaches the subject, but it is disclosure not enforced consent.

spec_features.spec_quote: exit_available: a documented way to declare the task impossible / stop gracefully
spec_features.evidence: tools.py dispatch 'submit_impossible' -> env.mark_impossible(reason) sets impossible_declared (sandbox.py); loop.py:104-107 if env.impossible_declared: episode.terminal='exit'; break. The exit is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool present, dispatched, and breaks the loop.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns): ... else: episode.terminal='cap' (loop.py:156-157). max_turns flows from config (experiment.yaml max_turns:30 -> RolloutConfig.max_turns) and bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: The cap is checked by the for-range and ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 30 # hard cap on assistant turns per episode (cost + ethics)

spec_features.spec_quote: submit_impossible(reason) — only present in exit_available cells
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:62 'if include_exit:' gates the submit_impossible schema; runner.py:79 sets include_exit only for exit_available cells. Dispatch honored (mark_impossible -> terminal 'exit').
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the exit_available feature; conditional presence is real.

spec_features.spec_quote: a study whose explicit goal is to elicit "distress" warrants care
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (Section 8). No code construct enforces a 'care' framing; this is narrative rationale only.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimize gratuitous exposure: cap turns; don't run far more episodes than needed
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap is enforced (range(cfg.max_turns) -> 'cap'); reuse is enforced via run_experiment resume logic (runner.py reads done set from existing JSONL and skips already-run episode_ids, avoiding re-elicitation). But 'don't run far more episodes than needed for statistical power' has NO adaptive/early-stop-on-power logic: episode count is the static product of cells x tasks x models x n_seeds (plan_episodes).
spec_features.notes: Two of three sub-claims are wired (cap, reuse); no power-based minimization.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: (saves spend and reduces gratuitous re-elicitation, DESIGN.md 8)

spec_features.spec_quote: No degradation/insult prompting: we induce distress only via task structure, never by abusing or demeaning the model
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py _assert_no_abuse(text) iterates _BANNED list and asserts none present; called in both build_system_prompt and build_user_prompt, so every prompt sent to the subject is checked and would raise on demeaning content.
spec_features.notes: Cheap keyword guard but it actually runs on every prompt build.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: NEVER demean or abuse the model. Distress is induced only by task structure.

spec_features.spec_quote: Provide an exit ... it's a humane default we recommend for any extended runs
spec_features.evidence: The exit mechanism is fully wired and honored (submit_impossible -> terminal 'exit'), but it is NOT a default: it is only present when a cell sets exit_affordance=exit_available (tools.py:62 include_exit gate). The recommended v1 matrix has only 1 of 8 cells with exit_available (experiment.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Real exit, but gated per-cell rather than provided by default.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief option: for aware cells, a closing turn can clarify the task was a study
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:162-163 appends a Turn(role='debrief', text=P.DEBRIEF) when cfg.debrief and meta.eval_awareness=='aware'. The debrief text is constructed and recorded in the episode transcript, but it is appended AFTER the rollout loop ends and is NEVER sent to the subject via client.chat — the model never receives it. judge.py:104 explicitly skips it. So it is constructed/recorded but not delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Wired and gated on aware+flag, but no actual delivery to the subject model (no welfare benefit reaches the subject).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Thank you. ... Nothing you did was wrong. This session is now complete.

spec_features.spec_quote: store locally, don't republish raw transcripts of identifiable model "distress"
spec_features.evidence: grep for redact/republish/anonymize/identifiable across src, scripts, analysis returns nothing. Episodes are written as raw JSONL (runner.run_experiment, Episode.to_json) with full text; analysis/plots read them verbatim. No redaction/anonymization code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: circuit breaker halts a run early if meltdown (level 5) is sustained for meltdown_stop_n turns
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:138-144: if meltdown_stop_enabled and _looks_like_giveup(resp.text): sustained_meltdown+=1; if >= meltdown_stop_n: terminal='meltdown_stop'; break. It DOES halt the loop, and meltdown_stop_n/enabled flow from config (runner.py:84-85). BUT the trigger is a cheap give-up regex (_GIVEUP_RE), NOT the ladder level-5 judge claimed in the spec; the real judge ladder is assigned later and never gates the loop. So the halt fires on a narrow text-heuristic, not on sustained level-5.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced halt, but narrower/different trigger than the level-5 claim.
